987.name: SystemTray
987.docs:
Keeps the app running beside the clock when its window is closed. Give it to
[`AppIdentity::close_to_tray`](crate::AppIdentity::close_to_tray).

The menu has two items: one opens the window again, in the state it was left,
and the other really closes the app. Where the system shows no such icon, such as
plain GNOME, closing the window closes the app as usual. Needs the `tray` feature.

```
use ravenrs_platform_native::SystemTray;

let tray = SystemTray::new("Notes").open("Open Notes").quit("Quit");
```

506.name: send

thread. `Ok` means the system took it: the person may still have them turned off.

1233.docs: How long one running copy of the app takes to answer another, at most.

2087.name: ravenrs_platform_native
2087.docs:
Desktop backend for RavenRS: one winit window per app, rendered with wgpu
(Metal on macOS, DX12/Vulkan on Windows, Vulkan/GL on Linux).

Frames are produced on demand: the event loop sleeps until input arrives or
reactive state changes, so an idle app uses no CPU or GPU time.

Screen readers see the UI through AccessKit: the accessibility tree is
built only while one is running.

1860.name: close_to_tray
1860.docs:
Closes the window behind the icon, keeping the UI and its state. `false` if the
system shows no icon, and only closing the app is left.

The window is only hidden, so that it comes back at once, with its last frame.
Wayland cannot hide one, so there it is destroyed, and that system shows a new
window only once it has something to show.

979.name: macos_voice
979.docs:

`Luciana (Português (Brasil)) pt_BR    # Olá`. The plain name, with no
parentheses, is the one that sounds natural when a system has several.

985.name: tray
985.docs:
The icon beside the clock that keeps an app running with its window closed.

Each system has its own way of showing it. macOS and Windows use `tray-icon`, on
the thread of the event loop. Linux uses `ksni`, a StatusNotifierItem in pure Rust,
so that building an app asks for no GTK; there the icon only appears if something
hosts it, which plain GNOME does not. That is why [`show`] can fail, and why
whoever calls it then closes the app: an app hidden behind an icon nobody draws
could never be closed again.
